subjectiveCriteria: Use clear, plain, practical, straightforward language, technically authoritative, and accessible, empathetic and understanding.
Target an education level of high school graduate or below.
Include at least two relevant, authoritative external sources, such as official documentation, government agencies, universities, or recognized research organizations.
Include at least two factual statistics when appropriate. Every statistic must have a direct link to its original authoritative source.
Never invent statistics, citations, URLs, research findings, or source claims. If a reliable source cannot be verified, omit the statistic.
Place the source link in the same paragraph as the statistic or factual claim it supports.
Use real, working URLs. Do not use placeholder links.
Add links to other blog posts or other content on the web site.  Do not use fabricated or falsified links.  Use real links to real pages.
Content is becoming repetitive.  Ensure you vary your language, tropes, analogies, phrases, starts, finishes, etc. between posts.
The blog post must make sense when read aloud, or if used as a script for a podcast.
Do not use text or html based tables, charts, or other formatting.
Do not invent metrics, prices, statistics, laws, results, client details, or product features
Do not provide individualized legal, financial, medical, or cybersecurity advice
Optimize for search and answer engines
End the article with a Call to Action (CTA) to contact us.
